articles.title: X shares more insight into penalties impacting post reach
articles.summary: X has broadened its Under The Hood transparency tool, which last month began letting users see penalties and restrictions applied to their posts or accounts. The update now adds visibility into government-related content filtering, showing whether an account or specific posts had their reach limited because of compliance with local laws in a particular country, following a legal demand. Previously the tool only displayed labels applied to accounts and posts over the prior month; now it also flags country-specific withholding tied to legal requirements. X says the expansion responds to positive feedback on transparency around content filtering. The added detail is meant to help users understand shadowban concerns and clarify actual post and profile performance, which matters especially for creators in X's monetization program, though any user could benefit from seeing exactly which labels or restrictions have hit their account. Eligibility for these insights requires an account to be at least one year old and to have published more than 10 posts in the previous month.
articles.li_summary: X expanded its Under The Hood feature to show users whether their posts or accounts had visibility limited due to government-mandated content compliance, including which country issued the legal demand, available to accounts over one year old with 10+ monthly posts.

articles.title: Snapchat report examines the rise of microdramas
articles.summary: Snapchat has released a report examining the growing popularity of microdramas, short episodic soap opera-style video series that align with short-form content consumption habits. Based on an Ipsos study of 3,000 people across the US, UK and Saudi Arabia conducted earlier this year, the report found Snapchat users are notably more engaged with this format than average consumers, with familiarity levels 1.4 times higher than competitors. Specifically, 64% of Snapchatters know at least one short drama platform compared to 42% of non-Snapchatters, and 42% of Snapchat users watch microdramas daily, with consumption increasing over time. The report attributes much of the format's appeal to communal viewing, since most microdrama fans share clips and discuss episodes with friends, making the content valuable for creators seeking engaged audiences. Snapchat suggests this creates promotional opportunities for brands, including sponsoring short drama creators or producing branded short dramas built around popular romance and thriller themes, genres that don't require high production budgets. The report also notes Snapchatters are more likely than average users to pay for subscription access to microdrama creator content.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat's new Ipsos-based report of 3,000 users across the US, UK and Saudi Arabia finds 42% of Snapchatters watch soap opera-style microdramas daily, with 64% familiar with at least one short drama platform versus 42% of non-Snapchatters.

articles.title: Pinterest offers predictive optimization for Performance+
articles.summary: Pinterest introduced a campaign optimization score inside Ads Manager, giving advertisers a single metric that predicts how well their campaign setup will perform based on alignment with best practices. The score evaluates four elements: adoption of Performance+ tools for targeting, budget and bidding alignment; variety of creative assets to reach broader audiences; use of broad targeting so Performance+ can select optimal audiences; and consistent budget pacing to support system learning. Pinterest recommends running at least three ad formats per ad group and five or more distinct ads to give its AI enough signals to identify what works across different audiences. To help meet these requirements, Pinterest offers Performance+ creative, a tool that automatically remixes existing assets into new formats and variations. Pinterest also advised advertisers to keep conversion data current and ensure product feeds and catalogs are updated to reflect shopping trends. The move builds on Pinterest's broader push to strengthen Performance+, which the company said in March delivered a 10% improvement in cost-per-click and cost-per-action compared to standard campaign setups.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest launched a campaign optimization score in Ads Manager that grades ad setups on four factors to boost alignment with its AI-driven Performance+ system, following March data showing 10% better CPC and CPA.

articles.title: Threads advertisers will no longer need an Instagram account
articles.summary: Meta announced that beginning in September 2026, advertisers will no longer need matching usernames across Threads and Instagram to launch ads on Threads, and businesses without any Instagram presence will be able to create Threads ads directly through native Threads profiles. Previously, Threads ad creation was tied to Instagram identity, requiring advertisers to maintain consistent branding across both apps before promoting content on Threads. This change reflects Threads' growth to roughly 500 million users, positioning it as a standalone advertising platform with an audience that behaves differently from Instagram users rather than simply overlapping with it. Meta has already begun separating the two platforms in other ways, including removing Instagram graph insights from the Threads onboarding process, though Instagram engagement signals are still used to gauge likely interest for Threads users. This latest update signals Meta's broader push to treat Threads as an independent product with its own advertising ecosystem rather than an extension of Instagram. The company noted the rollout will happen gradually, meaning not all advertisers will have immediate access to these new ad-creation options right away.
articles.li_summary: Starting September 2026, Meta will let advertisers run Threads ads without matching Instagram usernames or even holding an Instagram account, using native Threads profiles instead, as the app's user base reaches 500 million.

articles.title: Snapchat adds new AI features including chat-to-song
articles.summary: Snapchat introduced a batch of AI features exclusively for its Lens+ subscription tier, aimed at boosting engagement and paid subscriptions. The headline addition is Snap-to-song, which lets users pick a chat message and a music genre, then converts that text into a full AI-generated song, tapping into a trend already popular on short-form video platforms. Also new is AI Photoshoot, which automatically fixes flawed photos, such as blinking, bad lighting or awkward expressions, without requiring a retake. AI Remix allows users to reimagine an existing image in a completely different scenario or setting, while a separate update introduces AI-enhanced font styles like bubble text, fuzzy textures and spray-paint effects, plus the ability to remix stickers into new visual styles. Separately, Snapchat+ subscribers can now build a customizable 3D model of their home to display on Snap Map, choosing a location and appearance. These additions expand Snapchat's paid tools lineup, though they arrive as the company also works to curb AI content overload, having adjusted its Spotlight algorithm last month to reduce visibility of fully AI-generated videos.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat rolled out several AI-powered tools for Lens+ subscribers, including Snap-to-song (turning chat messages into AI-generated songs), AI Photoshoot photo touch-ups, AI Remix scene re-creation, and new AI-enhanced fonts and stickers.

articles.title: Creator content preferred in AI recommendations: Here’s what the numbers say
articles.summary: The Interactive Advertising Bureau's "Creator Signal" report surveyed 2,200 recent AI-shopping users across the US, UK, Australia, Mexico and India in May 2026 and found 80% are comfortable relying on AI for purchase recommendations, with 56% preferring when those recommendations cite creator or influencer content. That preference splits sharply by generation: 65% of Gen Z and millennials want creator citations versus just 34% of boomers, with Gen X roughly split at 53%. Yet citing creators doesn't necessarily drive sales — only 29% of younger respondents and 12% of boomers said creator mentions actually increased purchase likelihood, with consumer ratings, subject-matter experts, retailers and brand content generally outranking influencers on that metric. Creators are seen as most useful early in the shopping journey, particularly for finding value/pricing (38%) and discovering new brands (32%), but far less helpful at checkout (15%) or final decisions (21%). Everyday consumers and professional reviewers are trusted far more than lifestyle influencers, journalists or celebrities, with credibility track record (49%) and consistency (40%) mattering more than follower count (21%).
articles.li_summary: IAB's new "Creator Signal" report, based on 2,200 shoppers across the US, UK, Australia, Mexico and India surveyed in May 2026, finds 80% comfortable with AI shopping recommendations and 56% preferring when those results cite creator or influencer reviews.

articles.title: LinkedIn tests Network tab to encourage engagement among connections
articles.summary: LinkedIn is trialing a Network tab as an alternative to its main feed, announced last Friday by Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan. The tab would show updates exclusively from accounts a user has explicitly connected with or followed, rather than the algorithmically curated mix currently shown on the main feed. Srinivasan framed the test as part of LinkedIn's push toward "real connection with real people," a response to growing concerns about engagement pods artificially inflating post metrics and AI-generated content flooding user feeds. This isn't LinkedIn's first attempt at reworking feed discovery: last year the platform tested several alternative feed formats to boost app usage, and in June it piloted topic-based suggested feeds meant to surface trending conversations. Neither of those experiments led to a wider rollout, suggesting they failed to gain sufficient traction internally or with users. Whether the Network tab succeeds where those attempts didn't may depend on whether users want a more direct, connection-only view rather than LinkedIn's broader discovery-focused approach. No timeline for wider release has been shared.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is testing a new Network tab, announced by Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan last Friday, showing only updates from users' direct connections and follows to counter engagement pods and AI-generated feed content.

articles.title: Meta expands Muse agent connections, launches Muse for Mac
articles.summary: Meta has expanded its Muse agentic AI tool with two updates. Muse for Mac, released late last week, allows Mac users to connect their Muse agent directly to their computer, with explicit permission, so it can organize downloads folders, locate lost files, and summarize messages and notes. Separately, Meta introduced Muse Connectors, a system letting third-party developers apply to link their apps to Muse and potentially get listed in a Muse directory, expanding the range of tasks users can delegate to the agent through connected accounts. Meta says these moves are meant to broaden Muse's usefulness and make it more attractive to everyday consumers. However, some users have already noticed Muse reading their DMs on Mac and suggesting actions based on private conversations, which Meta says only happens with explicit permission but could still feel invasive. The company also faces a broader challenge in convincing users that granting Muse access to sensitive data, like messages or financial transactions, is worth the convenience, especially since many of the tasks Muse automates are ones people already enjoy doing themselves.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Muse for Mac, letting its AI agent directly access a user's computer to organize files or summarize messages, alongside new Muse Connectors that let developers link third-party apps into the Muse agent system.

articles.title: LinkedIn ditches post enhancement, launches Post Proofreader
articles.summary: LinkedIn quietly removed its AI post enhancement tool last month and has now launched a replacement called Post Proofreader, available to eligible Premium members. Unlike the old feature, which let users regenerate posts using AI in-stream, Post Proofreader focuses on refining existing drafts by showing suggested edits with inline change tracking, letting users review and choose whether to accept each change. Premium subscribers get three enhancement options to polish language and presentation without creating entirely new content that doesn't reflect their own voice. The shift comes as LinkedIn cracks down on AI-generated content: last month it introduced an "AI slop" reporting tool for posts, which was used more than one million times within three weeks of launch, and this month expanded that reporting option to comments as well. By rebranding enhancement as proofreading, LinkedIn is signaling a broader strategic shift toward positioning AI as an editing aid rather than a content-generation shortcut, responding directly to growing user frustration with inauthentic, AI-produced posts flooding the platform.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn has replaced its AI-powered post enhancement tool with Post Proofreader, a Premium-only feature offering three editing options that suggest inline changes for users to approve rather than generating entirely new post content.

articles.title: YouTube executives share strategies on channel pivoting
articles.summary: YouTube Creator Liaison Rene Ritchie and Global Content Strategy Lead Kyle Monahan shared guidance for creators and brands considering a content pivot, using the example of a gaming creator wanting to switch games. Monahan said the first step is determining the root cause: whether the audience has lost interest or the creator has lost passion. Ritchie emphasized that creators often overestimate how much their audience follows them personally versus their specific topic, citing GTA 5 content as an example where viewers may be there for the game itself, not the creator's personality. Both stressed identifying a channel's unique selling proposition, voice, or tone, since strong personal branding makes pivoting easier regardless of subject matter. Monahan recommended mapping out clear end goals and using Google Trends to spot pivot opportunities, while also weighing competition levels, noting that smaller, underserved niches can generate substantial views for creators offering a unique perspective, even without chasing the largest trending categories. YouTube also offers a dedicated strategic guide with questions to help creators plan pivots effectively.
articles.li_summary: YouTube executives Rene Ritchie and Kyle Monahan outlined a framework for creators pivoting content focus, urging them to identify whether audiences follow them or their topic before switching niches, such as changing gaming titles.

articles.title: X shares guidance on effective promotions in the app
articles.summary: X, formerly Twitter, has refreshed its Business blog to consolidate strategy guides and resources designed to help marketers build more effective ad campaigns on the platform. Despite losing some cultural influence in recent years, X maintains over 550 million monthly active users and continues to serve as a key hub for industry discussions and reaching decision-makers who drive purchasing decisions. The updated resource hub includes several concise, one-page overviews covering different aspects of X advertising. Two standout guides highlighted include a breakdown of X ads best practices, offering practical tips on structuring campaigns for better performance, and a separate overview identifying key calendar events and moments brands can align their promotions with to boost engagement. Together, these resources provide marketers with actionable, easy-to-digest guidance on optimizing ad content and timing to drive stronger audience response. For brands still active on X or considering the platform, these updated guides offer a quick reference to refine targeting and messaging strategies without needing to sift through lengthy documentation.
articles.li_summary: X revamped its Business blog with updated strategy guides, including one-page overviews on ad best practices and key promotional events, aimed at helping brands improve campaign performance across its 550 million monthly active users.

articles.title: Wonderful Pistachios spotlights first NIL roster in social campaign
articles.summary: Wonderful Pistachios launched "Don't Hold Back All-Stars," its first name, image and likeness campaign, signing seven college athletes spanning six sports and all Power Four conferences. The roster includes Maryland track star Quincy Wilson, Duke's Deron Rippey Jr., UNC's Deus Stanislaus, Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis, Florida softball player Taylor Shumaker, USC basketball's Jazzy Davidson and volleyball's London Wijay. Created in-house by The Wonderful Agency, the campaign runs through the 2026-27 sports season with content rolling out across fall, winter and spring. Rather than centering the product as in past ads, the creative takes cues from brands like Nike, using a trading-card-inspired visual style built around each athlete's personality and sport, according to Chief Creative Officer Bobby Pearce. The push extends the brand's 2025 "The Don't Hold Back Snack" platform, which focused on destigmatizing snacking through out-of-home ads. It also follows last fall's national campaign with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, as Wonderful Pistachios deepens its sports marketing strategy amid a better-for-you snacks market projected to grow from $118.1 billion in 2026 to $207.5 billion by 2034.
articles.li_summary: Wonderful Pistachios debuted its first NIL athlete roster with "Don't Hold Back All-Stars," a social campaign featuring seven college stars across six sports and all Power Four conferences, running through the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Meta streamlines creator, brand tie-ups with new marketing hub
articles.summary: Meta unveiled the global rollout of its Creator Marketing Hub, announced via company blog and at IAB's first Global Creator Week, adding features like expanded discovery filters, improved content recommendations, ad readiness editing tools, and built-in partnership messaging, with updates continuing through the rest of 2026. Facebook creators now join Instagram creators in Meta's Creator Marketplace API, giving advertisers single-integration access to both platforms, while the Content Discovery API expands to surface top-performing organic creator content. Meta's AI business assistant is now embedded in the hub, letting advertisers chat to find creators and get recommendations, and Partnership Ads gain support from the Meta Ads MCP connector, enabling management through third-party AI agents. Instagram will also get Live video ads on September 29, matching a feature already live on Facebook, letting brands amplify creators' live streams as Partnership Ads. The moves come as IAB data shows creator ad spending reached $37 billion in 2025 and 45% of consumer purchases are now influenced by creator recommendations, while Meta's Q2 revenue rose 28% to $60.8 billion.
articles.li_summary: Meta globally launched its Creator Marketing Hub with expanded APIs, AI business assistant integration, and new discovery/messaging tools, rolling out through 2026 as creator ad spend hit $37 billion in 2025.

articles.title: Facebook Pages get charged for link posts
articles.summary: Meta is widening a restriction first tested in December 2025 that caps certain Facebook Pages at two link posts per month unless they subscribe to Meta One for Business, a paid plan launched this week. The subscription already offers Instagram accounts a limited number of monthly link posts on feed posts and Reels, depending on tier, and Facebook link access looks set to become another paid perk, though it isn't officially listed yet. Publisher Pages remain exempt to keep outside content flowing into the app, but other business Pages are increasingly seeing pop-up alerts warning of the two-link cap. Meta says it's testing whether added link volume is valuable enough for users to pay for. The practical impact may be limited: Meta's Q1 2026 Widely Viewed Content report shows only 1.3% of viewed posts in the U.S. contained an outside link, down from 9.8% in 2022, meaning link posts already get minimal organic reach on Facebook regardless of this new restriction.
articles.li_summary: Meta is expanding a test that limits non-paying Facebook Pages to two link posts per month, pushing more brands toward its new Meta One for Business paid subscription tiers.

articles.title: Reddit offers insights from its Health Summit event
articles.summary: Reddit hosted its inaugural Health Summit in New York on September 4, sharing data that highlights its growing role as a health resource and outlining opportunities for healthcare marketers. The platform reported over 36 billion views on healthcare-related conversations in the past year, with 46% of U.S. doctors now active on the app. In 2025 alone, users created 473 million posts connecting symptoms to potential conditions, drawing on first-hand diagnosis experiences. Additional findings showed 70% of women's reproductive health audiences felt more prepared for medical conversations after using Reddit, 61% of U.S. health information seekers treat the platform as a final check before acting, and 90% of views in gender-focused communities came from women-oriented spaces. Reddit also noted that GLP-1 medication discussions extend beyond health topics into communities like Healthy Living, Career Advice, Travel, Entertainment, Family & Relationships, and Business & Finance, suggesting brands need broader outreach strategies. The data reinforces Reddit's positioning as a source of crowd-sourced, lived-experience health insights that complement clinical information.
articles.li_summary: Reddit's first Health Summit in New York on Sept. 4 revealed that health conversations drew 36 billion views in the past year, 46% of U.S. doctors are active users, and 473 million posts in 2025 linked symptoms to possible conditions.

articles.title: Meta shares holiday 2026 planning guides
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out a fresh set of holiday planning resources aimed at helping marketers prepare for Q4 shopping season strategy. The release includes several distinct guides: an AI-focused overview explaining how to leverage Meta's ad tools, a dedicated agency guide, and a creative explainer for building holiday ad campaigns. For small and medium-sized businesses, Meta published a guide packed with statistics on how consumers use its apps for gift research and shopping engagement, alongside a checklist designed to help SMBs capitalize on holiday opportunities, plus practical tips on ad creation and campaign timing. For larger, more advanced advertisers, Meta released a separate playbook featuring additional data on shopping behaviors across its app family, along with guidance on prioritizing ad setup and a checklist for optimizing product listings ahead of peak shopping periods. These materials expand Meta's existing Festive Season Insights Center, reinforcing the company's push to position its platforms as central tools for holiday product discovery, research, and purchase decisions as brands finalize Q4 budgets and campaigns.
articles.li_summary: Meta released a new batch of holiday 2026 planning guides for marketers, covering AI tools, agency strategy, creative tips, SMB checklists, and an advanced advertiser playbook with shopping behavior stats.

articles.title: Reddit SMB guide offers holiday planning tips
articles.summary: Reddit has launched a new 2026 Small Business Holiday Insights guide aimed at SMBs, focusing on how users discover products and make purchasing decisions on the platform. The 11-page report covers gift research trends, optimal posting times, and the most-searched product categories to help marketers target relevant sectors. Key data points include that approximately 75% of Reddit users turn to the platform for honest, unfiltered reviews when researching holiday gifts, and nearly 50% prefer shopping from local or independent retailers over larger chains. Notably, mentions of "small business" within the r/gifts community increased 120% year-over-year in 2025, signaling growing interest in supporting smaller sellers during the holidays. The guide also demonstrates that community discussions on Reddit influence purchase validation, with most users willing to pay more for products recommended within Reddit threads. Additional sections address Black Friday shopping behavior and other seasonal trends. The full report is available on Reddit's business site for marketers planning their end-of-year campaigns.
articles.li_summary: Reddit released an 11-page holiday planning guide for small businesses, revealing that 75% of users trust the platform for unfiltered gift reviews and mentions of "small business" in r/gifts rose 120% year-over-year in 2025.

articles.title: X adds in-stream stock trading
articles.summary: X has rolled out its Cashtag Partner Program in the U.S., extending the platform's existing Cashtags feature to enable direct trading from within the app. Previously, X's April update linked cashtag mentions to embedded stock market data, but users couldn't act on that information without leaving the platform. Now, tapping a Cashtag lets users connect to their accounts on partner brokerages, currently Interactive Brokers, Moomoo, Gemini, Kraken, and Coinbase, to buy or trade stocks and cryptocurrencies in response to real-time discussions and market news appearing in their feed. This move builds on X's existing U.S. payments infrastructure and pushes further toward Elon Musk's long-stated "everything app" ambition, where X eventually handles all financial activity for users, potentially positioning it as an alternative to traditional banks. By tying trading capability directly to conversation and news flow, X aims to capture user intent at the moment interest is highest, though it remains uncertain whether users will trust the platform enough to route significant financial activity through it.
articles.li_summary: X launched its Cashtag Partner Program in the U.S., letting users tap stock ticker mentions in posts to trade directly through partner brokerages including Interactive Brokers, Moomoo, Gemini, Kraken, and Coinbase.

articles.title: Report highlights the value of creator-led collabs on Instagram
articles.summary: Emplifi's review of more than 520,000 Instagram posts across 3,791 brand profiles between January and June 2026 found that creator-led collaboration posts significantly outperform standard brand content and brand-initiated collabs. Instagram supports two collaboration formats: "owned" collaborations, where a brand publishes a post and tags a creator, and "accepted" collaborations, where a creator publishes the post and invites a brand to co-sponsor it. Emplifi's data shows 73% of brands now use Instagram's collaboration tools, but it's the creator-initiated posts that deliver the biggest results, generating more than five times the amplification of non-collaboration posts within ecommerce and retail categories specifically, with strong share and repost gains across other verticals too. This trend may be tied to Meta's expanded affiliate program, announced in March, which lets creators pick products to promote directly within Reels and earn commissions, incentivizing more creator-driven sponsored content. Emplifi also found that while collaborations boost performance across all content formats, Reels see the largest gains, reinforcing that creators, who specialize in short-form video, are better positioned to drive engagement than brands publishing solo.
articles.li_summary: Emplifi analyzed over 520,000 Instagram posts from 3,791 brand profiles and found creator-published collaboration posts outperform brand posts, driving over 5x the amplification of non-collab content in ecommerce and retail.

articles.title: Meta adds simplified third-party AI support to WhatsApp
articles.summary: Meta has introduced WhatsApp Business Tools MCP, a new integration process designed to help businesses connect their preferred third-party AI tools directly into the WhatsApp Business Platform. Instead of requiring developers to manually code automated systems, marketers can now describe in plain language the type of agent, response system, or workflow they want, and their chosen AI tool will generate the technical steps needed to build it within WhatsApp. This covers a range of business functions, including creating customer-facing marketing templates, setting up automated reply systems, and building agent profiles for handling customer queries. The move is aimed at lowering the technical barrier for brands wanting to use WhatsApp as a customer service and engagement channel, particularly as the app's usage continues to grow amid a broader shift toward private messaging over public social media interaction. By simplifying AI integration, Meta is positioning WhatsApp as a more viable platform for always-on customer support, potentially helping businesses respond faster to queries and maintain more direct, continuous engagement with their audience without needing in-house coding expertise.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched WhatsApp Business Tools MCP, letting brands connect third-party AI chatbot tools to build automated agent profiles, marketing templates, and response workflows via conversational requests instead of manual coding.

articles.title: LinkedIn offers tips on company targeting via Campaign Manager
articles.summary: LinkedIn has released guidance on using the Companies hub within Campaign Manager to help B2B marketers identify and target key decision-makers more effectively. The feature tracks which businesses' representatives engage with a brand's organic posts and paid ads on the platform. LinkedIn's four-step framework starts with uploading a company list or connecting a CRM to merge first-party data with platform insights. Next, marketers use the Companies dashboard to monitor which accounts engage with content, filtering by engagement level and job seniority to confirm they're reaching actual decision-makers rather than junior staff. Third, brands should segment companies by engagement stage, retargeting those showing high ad interaction and building lookalike audiences from CRM data. Finally, marketers track engagement with follow-up campaigns to gauge each account's position in the purchase funnel and adjust strategy accordingly. LinkedIn recommends starting with a small group of accounts resembling top customers, connecting CRM data, watching for engagement signals, then directing subsequent campaigns at responsive companies to nurture them toward conversion, ultimately improving targeting precision and ad performance.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn published a four-step guide for using the Companies hub in Campaign Manager, helping marketers track account-level engagement, filter by job seniority, and retarget high-intent decision-makers with CRM data.

articles.title: Threads adds more podcast promotion features
articles.summary: Threads announced a broad update to its podcast features on Wednesday, expanding on tools it began rolling out last November like podcast profile cards and custom thumbnails. The new additions include profile and post banners displaying a podcast's logo and details, an episode picker that turns podcast links into tappable cards, and support for transcripts, video, and guest cards to spotlight specific episodes—transcripts had been spotted in testing last month. Creators and guests can now opt into automatic episode reminders to prompt sharing, while listeners can save favorite episodes directly within the app. Threads is also introducing Podcast Insights, giving creators data on engagement, clicks, and saves to track how their content performs. The company says these updates build on Threads' existing role as a space where podcast conversations happen organically, aiming to make it easier for creators to promote shows and for users to discuss them. The push comes as podcast listenership keeps climbing, with Edison Research reporting that 58% of Americans tuned into podcasts in 2026.
articles.li_summary: Threads launched a new set of podcast promotion tools on Wednesday, including profile and post banners, episode link cards, transcript and guest cards, episode reminders, save options, and creator performance insights, as it pushes to become the top hub for podcast discussion.

articles.title: TikTok announces featured creators for Hispanic Heritage Month
articles.summary: TikTok has launched a series of in-app activations to mark Hispanic Heritage Month, which runs from September 15 to October 15. The centerpiece is a creator showcase featuring figures such as journalist Fernando Hurtado, musician Jasmine Wesley, and comedian Eric Sedeño, chosen to represent storytelling, tradition, and lived experience within Hispanic and Latino communities on the app. TikTok will publish individual interviews with each featured creator through its official TikTok Creators profile, while broader community content will be organized under hashtags including #HispanicTikTok, #LatinTikTok, #HispanicHeritageTikTokContest, and #CasaTikTok. The platform is also running a competition designed to boost user participation and engagement throughout the month-long celebration. TikTok framed the initiative as part of its ongoing effort to highlight historically marginalized groups and demonstrate how the app helps amplify diverse voices and cultural narratives. This year’s push builds on the platform’s broader strategy of using cultural observances to strengthen ties with specific user communities, reinforcing TikTok’s positioning as a space where identity-driven storytelling can reach large, engaged audiences.
articles.li_summary: TikTok kicked off Hispanic Heritage Month (Sept. 15–Oct. 15) by spotlighting creators like journalist Fernando Hurtado, musician Jasmine Wesley and comedian Eric Sedeño, alongside themed hashtags and a new engagement competition.

articles.title: Snapchat report highlights users’ political engagement
articles.summary: Ahead of the November U.S. midterms, Snapchat released a civic engagement report based on an Alter Agents survey of more than 1,000 users aged 18 to 45, aiming to attract political advertisers. The data shows 78% of Snapchat users intend to vote, making them 1.2 times more likely to vote than non-users. Political ads on the platform are influential too: 80% of respondents said promotions introduced them to candidates or causes they didn't previously know, and 74% said ads prompted them to research candidates further. Peer influence remains strong, with 66% discovering political information through close social circles and 64% trusting peer perspectives over traditional news outlets. Snapchat users are also 1.4 times more likely than non-users to engage with cause- or candidate-related ads, at 83%. This builds on Snapchat's history of voter mobilization efforts, having driven 450,000 voter registrations in 2018 and 1.2 million in 2020 through in-app prompts, reinforcing its case as a valuable channel for political outreach.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat published a new report from Alter Agents, surveying over 1,000 users aged 18-45, showing 78% plan to vote in the midterms and 83% actively engage with political ads, as it pitches itself for election ad spend.

articles.title: Meta adds more creator partnership tools
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Meta officially launched its Creator Marketing hub, first previewed in June, merging brand-creator discovery and outreach into a single platform. New features include discovery filters with predicted affiliate content search, objective-based content recommendations, one-click ad creation from creator listings, content-level permissions with expiration dates, and ad editing tools letting brands remove copyrighted music or stickers from creator content. Partnership messaging is now built directly into the hub, so brands can move from discov
articles.li_summary: Meta launched its Creator Marketing hub on Tuesday, consolidating discovery, outreach, and ad-creation tools into one interface, while also expanding creator APIs and rolling out Instagram live video ads on September 29.

articles.title: Meta announces Edits Plus paid subscription tier
articles.summary: Meta is building a paid subscription tier called Edits Plus for its Edits video editing app, which competes with ByteDance's CapCut. The tier was revealed in a slide from a broader announcement about Meta's new Meta One Business subscription packages, and will be offered either bundled within those business packages or as its own standalone subscription. Edits Plus will give users more storage for video projects and expanded access to Meta's AI-powered editing features, addressing capacity limits that currently restrict heavy users. Meta has long signaled it would eventually monetize AI add-ons within Edits, and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri explained in a July Stories Q&A that the AI models powering these tools are costly to run, so free access is currently capped by daily usage limits, with a subscription option in development to unlock higher usage caps. Meta has not disclosed pricing details or specified what the new usage thresholds will be once Edits Plus launches, leaving exact costs and limits still unknown.
articles.li_summary: Meta is developing "Edits Plus," a paid subscription tier for its Edits video editing app that offers expanded storage and greater access to AI-powered editing tools, available standalone or via Meta One Business packages.

articles.title: Meta launches Meta One for Business add-on packages
articles.summary: Meta introduced Meta One for Business, a new subscription lineup for brands, priced across tiers from $14.99 to $499 per month, bundling AI-powered tools, analytics and content features across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Higher tiers unlock competitive insights comparing up to 10 rival brands on Instagram, extended audience history data beyond the current 90-day limit, and custom audience insights showing non-followers who engage with content on Facebook. Content scheduling gets upgraded with posting-time recommendations and bulk Instagram uploads. A long-requested feature, links within Instagram posts and Reels, arrives in limited form: Advanced subscribers ($49.99/month) get 4 links each for posts and Reels monthly, Expert subscribers ($149) get 8, and Max subscribers ($499) get 12. Other perks include a bold Facebook Follow button for visibility, Verified Channels on WhatsApp, and a new AI chatbot called Meta business agent that answers customer messages on WhatsApp Business around the clock and offers engagement and lead-generation guidance. This expands Meta's subscription business, which already reportedly includes around 35 million Meta Verified users generating roughly $2 billion annually.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Meta One for Business, a tiered subscription line from $14.99 to $499 monthly offering AI tools, competitor insights on up to 10 brands, and limited Instagram post links.
